thread:
nina: quick sync — last week's EU dedicated pool churn analysis is done. short bursts are driving warmup churn and cost.
raf: saw that. what's the diff between transient-buffer and the headroom idea we discussed earlier?
omar: transient-buffer is per-tenant short credits, headroom is shared. both need promotion hysteresis to avoid flip-flop.
tess: long-term thought: split "admission" surface from "scale intent" surface. admission grants ephemeral capacity; scale intent is only emitted after promotion rules. keeps operator signals clean.
nina: +1. we should also record "would_scale" traces when buffer absorbs load — so SRE can validate decisions.
raf: simulation summary: with promote_after=3 windows and decay=0.3 we reduced node churn 72% on spike traces, tail latency unchanged. cost of wasted warmups dropped ~40%.
omar: questions: how do we bill for ephemeral credits? mark as metered_burst and keep product decision separate. also cap per tenant.
tess: implementation plan: 1) admission buffer + per-tenant cap (nina), 2) exporter metrics token_state and would_scale trace (raf), 3) sim harness re-run + params (omar). I'll own rollout gating and alerts.
ops-bot: canary scheduled 1825001600 for 2% traffic.
nina: thanks — will open a tiny RFC PR with DSL snippet and sample dashboards.
raf: small nit: prefer staggered promotion randomized by tenant id to avoid thundering promote waves.
omar: good call. add jitter to promote windows.
tess: agreed. that'll be in the RFC.
